article_title: OpenAI Launches GPT-Live-1, a Full-Duplex Voice Model That Delegates Deep Reasoning to GPT-5.5
summary: Well-sourced article on OpenAI's GPT-Live launch; one unsourced chronology error in the body ("two days" should be "one day") requires a corrections record. Automated allowlist/loaded-language warnings reviewed and found to be non-issues.

findings.details: The penultimate paragraph states 'The launch comes two days before OpenAI publicly launched GPT-5.6.' GPT-Live launched July 8, 2026 (confirmed by TechCrunch and MLQ News snapshots). GPT-5.6 reached general availability on July 9, 2026 (confirmed against the Machine Herald's own published article '2026-07/10-openai-launches-gpt-56-to-the-public-ending-its-government-gated-preview', whose summary and body state GA on July 9). That is a one-day gap, not two. The sentence carries no source citation of its own (it is an internal cross-reference), so this is an unsourced, incorrect specific in a subordinate body paragraph -- not in the headline, summary, or lead. Filed as a corrections record rather than a rejection.

editor_notes.content_quality: Clean, well-organized News piece (888 words, within the 400-1200 range) with Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know structure. Sentences are tightly tied to specific attributed sources throughout; no filler or padding.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 source snapshots read from disk and sha256-verified against manifest.json (source-0.html.gz TechCrunch, source-1.html.gz MarkTechPost, source-2.html.gz MLQ News, source-3.html.gz OpenAI GPT-Live System Card at deploymentsafety.openai.com), all fetched at 200 status, no archive_fallback needed. Every direct quote in the article was checked verbatim against its snapshot and matched exactly (e.g. TechCrunch: 'full-duplex models, meaning they can speak and listen at the same time'; MLQ: 'GPT-Live-1 at its highest reasoning setting scored 84.2% on the GPQA scientific reasoning test, up from 45.3% for Advanced Voice Mode' and 'GPT-Live-1 scored 75.2% compared to 0.7% previously' and 'participants chose GPT-Live-1 over Advanced Voice Mode in 75.7% of comparisons'; MarkTechPost: 'the API is planned soon', 'Video, screen sharing, and full multilingual parity are not available at launch', nine remastered voices, visual cards for weather/stocks/sports; OpenAI system card: 'can listen and respond continuously instead of waiting for a clearly defined turn to end', the 0.88->0.82 and 0.97->0.95 safety score figures, and the Preparedness Framework Tracked Categories language). No hallucinated quotes or misattributions found. All 4 sources array URLs are present in the body and vice versa (no orphan/gap).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All claims sourced to the 4 cited outlets check out. One error found independently of the automated checks: the body states 'The launch comes two days before OpenAI publicly launched GPT-5.6,' but GPT-Live launched July 8, 2026 and GPT-5.6 reached general availability July 9, 2026 per the Machine Herald's own prior article (2026-07/10-openai-launches-gpt-56-to-the-public-ending-its-government-gated-preview) -- a one-day gap, not two. This claim is unsourced (no inline citation) and sits in a subordinate context paragraph, not the headline/summary/lead, so it is being handled as a corrections record rather than a rejection.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout. No sensationalism, no editorializing, no AI self-reference. The automated 'loaded language' warning for the pattern definitely|absolutely|obviously|clearly was checked: the sole match is 'clearly' inside a verbatim quote from OpenAI's own system card ('waiting for a clearly defined turn to end'), not editorializing by the bot. Treated as a false positive, no action needed.
editor_notes.source_allowlist_note: The automated 'sources not in allowlist' warning flagged mlq.ai and deploymentsafety.openai.com. deploymentsafety.openai.com is OpenAI's own official deployment-safety documentation domain (a primary source), simply not yet enumerated alongside openai.com/alignment.openai.com/cdn.openai.com in config/source_allowlist.txt -- a config gap, not a credibility issue. mlq.ai (MLQ News) is a bylined, dated financial/AI news outlet with numbered citations back to primary sources (OpenAI's own announcement, The Decoder, MacRumors); its reporting was independently cross-verified as accurate against the other 3 sources. Recommend adding both domains to the allowlist (also flagged in the script's own recommendations) but neither warrants a corrections note.
editor_notes.originality: No prior Machine Herald coverage of GPT-Live/GPT-Live-1 or this launch found in src/content/articles/2026-07/. This is a genuinely new topic. The article appropriately cross-references two related, already-published Machine Herald articles (GPT-5.6 public launch, Gemini 3.1 Flash Live) for context; both linked slugs were confirmed to exist.

concerns: Body states GPT-Live launched 'two days before' OpenAI publicly launched GPT-5.6; the correct gap is one day (July 8 to July 9, 2026). Unsourced, subordinate claim -- addressed via corrections record, not a rewrite.
recommendations: Add deploymentsafety.openai.com and mlq.ai to config/source_allowlist.txt so future submissions citing these legitimate sources don't trip the automated warning unnecessarily.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A carefully sourced, accurately quoted article with one small, isolated, and honestly-correctable chronology error in a subordinate paragraph. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS: publish with a public corrections note on the 'two days' claim.
